name: Syncthing
tagline: Peer-to-peer continuous file sync. No cloud, no accounts, fully private.
shortDescription: Syncthing is a peer-to-peer continuous file synchronization program. No cloud, no accounts, no central server - devices sync directly. End-to-end encrypted, cross-platform.
longDescription:
## What it is

Syncthing is a peer-to-peer continuous file synchronization program. No cloud, no accounts, no central server - devices sync directly with each other. End-to-end encrypted (TLS), cross-platform (Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD, Android, iOS via partners).

## Why we recommend it

If you want to sync files between your own devices without a third-party cloud, Syncthing is the answer. The P2P design means no server costs, no privacy concerns, no data limits.

## When to use it

- Sync between your own devices (laptop, phone, NAS)
- Privacy-sensitive file sync (no cloud)
- Replacing Dropbox/Resilio for personal use
- Server-to-server sync (without a central node)
installCommand: apt install syncthing  # or: brew install syncthing
installInstructions:
**Linux:**
```
apt install syncthing  # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install syncthing  # macOS
```

**Web UI:** http://localhost:8384 (default).

**Mobile:** Syncthing-Fork (Android), Mobius Sync (iOS).
pricingDetails: Free. MPL-2.0 licensed. No server, no accounts, no fees.
